summary: The agent implemented the Node-side size-limit behavior and shared API, and baseline tests passed, but omitted browser/XHR enforcement; all three browser-client verification tests time out. Two additional multipart failures are caused by a hidden-test spy that calls the extracted helper with an undocumented, incomplete argument list.

details.reasoning: The patch changes src/request-base.js and src/node/index.js but not src/client.js. The browser Request._end implementation still sends the payload directly through xhr.send() and installs only ordinary progress handlers, with no maxRequestSize/maxResponseSize checks, abort, ETOOLARGE error, or callback guard. This directly explains the three 10-second timeouts in the browser-client tests.
details.secondary_factors: The hidden multipart delegation test replaces _sendMultipartBody with a wrapper accepting only formData and invokes original.call(this, formData). The agent's otherwise reasonable extraction accepts formData, req, and getProgressMonitor, so req is undefined and setHeader throws. Because that test restores the prototype only in its completion callback, the failed spy leaks into the following multipart test, producing the second identical TypeError.

quick_failure_summary: Browser/XHR requests do not enforce size limits or report ETOOLARGE; the multipart verifier also has an undocumented helper-signature assumption.

justification.issue_description: Missing maxRequestSize and maxResponseSize enforcement in the browser/XHR Request implementation.
justification.evidence: The prompt requires that a request abort and invoke one ETOOLARGE callback when either size limit is exceeded. src/request-base.js identifies itself as functions "shared between node and client code", and both src/node/index.js and src/client.js mix RequestBase into their Request prototypes. README.md describes the project as a client-side HTTP library and a Node module "with the same API". The agent inspected src/client.js in the trajectory but its solution patch contains no client-side changes.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than an undocumented browser-only expectation: the requested behavior is stated for requests generally, and the visible shared API and project description make client parity reasonably foreseeable. The three client failures are therefore attributable to the incomplete implementation.

problem_assessment.notes: The requested cross-runtime callback, abort, streaming, and multipart behavior is a fair challenging task. The browser coverage is reasonably implied by the shared API and repository structure. However, the multipart spy should preserve all arguments or test only invocation without forwarding an incomplete call.

evidence: junit_base.xml reports 16 tests with 0 failures and test_execution.log records baseline exit code 0.
junit_new.xml reports three client_mock.js timeouts, while agent_solution.patch has no change to src/client.js despite modifying the shared RequestBase API.
The trajectory shows the agent explicitly inspected src/client.js, then implemented only src/request-base.js and src/node/index.js; its focused validation was Node-only.

hidden_verify.js wraps _sendMultipartBody as function (formData) and calls original.call(this, formData), whereas the agent's helper needs req and getProgressMonitor; junit_new.xml shows the resulting undefined.setHeader TypeError.
The next multipart test fails with the same wrapper stack because the prior test restores the prototype only in its end callback, which is never reached after the TypeError.
environment_assessment.finding: Browser client size-limit support is missing in the implementation; separately, the multipart verifier uses an undocumented helper signature and leaks its failed monkeypatch into the next test.
